newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up, harvest delayed.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly up, harvest delayed.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed mostly higher, supported by harvest delays in North Dakota and signs of a slight pickup in export demand.

They noted that rains had slowed harvesting, could reduce test weights and may also lead to disease problems. Delays were, however, expected to be shortlived with some farmers possibly able to get back into the fields on Sunday.
Potential buyers of U.S. wheat in the export market during the next couple of weeks included Pakistan and Egypt.
September wheat closed 1-3/4 cents higher at $3.89-1/4 a bushel with other months up 1-1/4 to off 1-1/2 cents.

Volume was boosted by active September/December sp with Atwood bull spreading 1.5 million bushels while Cargill Investor Services took most of the other side of the trade. Options were also fairly active with interest centered on September calls with strike prices of $3.90 and $4.00.
Volume totalled 21.3 million bushels, up from 18.6 million on Thursday.
